skill.name: investigating-codebases
skill.description: Guides systematic exploration of unfamiliar repositories by mapping structure, finding entry points, tracing dependencies, and documenting how components work.
skill.summary: Investigate unfamiliar codebases with structured search, entry point discovery, dependency tracing, and evidence-based explanations.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code spans, and benign read-only directory inspection examples. One environment-file reference in SKILL.md is confirmed because it can lead agents to inspect secret-bearing .env files during investigation. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, network activity, or destructive command behavior was found.

remediation.issue: The guidance names real .env files as configuration targets.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer .env.example in examples and add a rule to avoid reading or quoting secret-bearing .env files unless the user explicitly approves.

content.value_statement: Unfamiliar repositories slow down feature work and incident response. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured process for codebase discovery.
actual_capabilities: Maps project structure and highlights common source, test, configuration, and tool directories.
Finds likely entry points for Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, Java, and web projects.
Guides keyword, file pattern, and implementation searches with Grep and Glob workflows.
Traces imports, function calls, request flows, and data transformations during feature analysis.
Provides templates for investigation summaries with locations, overview, key files, and execution flow.
limitations: It does not prove runtime behavior without tests or execution traces.
Scripts inspect local paths and should be run only on repositories the user controls.
It may miss framework-specific conventions outside the included references.
It should not read secret-bearing environment files unless the user explicitly approves.

use_cases.title: Onboard to a New Repository
use_cases.description: A developer can map folders, entry points, and key files before making changes.

use_cases.title: Answer Implementation Questions
use_cases.description: A reviewer can locate where a feature, route, or workflow is implemented and explain related files.

use_cases.title: Document Legacy Systems
use_cases.description: A documentation owner can turn scattered code paths into a concise architecture note.

prompt_templates.title: Map This Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this repository at a high level. Identify the project type, main directories, likely entry points, and important configuration files. Do not read secret files.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Find where [feature] is implemented. Search names and related concepts, then summarize primary files, related files, and the execution flow.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Request Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace how [request or command] moves through this codebase. Start from the entry point, follow handlers and services, and note validation and data access.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Architecture Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the architecture of this repository. Identify dominant patterns, dependency boundaries, test strategy, and risky coupling. Support each conclusion with file references.

output_examples.output: The answer names the authentication route, middleware, token service, and session storage. It explains request flow from submit to response.
The result lists build configuration, scripts, compilation steps, generated outputs, and development versus production differences.

output_examples.input: What kind of architecture is this?
output_examples.output: The report identifies layered service and repository patterns, then notes exceptions and related tests.

best_practices: Start with structure and documentation before reading deep implementation files.
Use narrow searches, then verify findings by reading related files.
Include file references and explain how components connect.
anti_patterns: Reading random files without a question or hypothesis.
Reporting a file location without explaining its role.
Inspecting secret files when sample configuration is enough.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when you need to understand where code lives, how a feature works, or how a repository is organized.

faq.question: Does this skill modify code?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for investigation, explanation, and documentation, not implementation changes.

faq.question: Which tools does it rely on?
faq.answer: It uses Read, Grep, Glob, and Task. It also includes optional local scripts for mapping and entry point discovery.

faq.question: Can it analyze any programming language?
faq.answer: It is language agnostic, with references for common web, API, frontend, backend, and package patterns.

faq.question: How should results cite evidence?
faq.answer: Results should include file paths, line references when available, and a short explanation of each file role.

faq.question: Is it safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: It reads local code and does not send data by itself. Avoid reading secret files and review script use first.
